topic: Mistral 4 beats Chinese models: run the receipt
thesis: Mistral's CEO said Large 4 beats the Chinese models; the morning the weights land, the receipt reads tied on coding at 48%, ahead on cyber at 51%, behind on the overall index at 26 -- and at 233 GB for the smallest quant, it does not fit on your gaming PC.
explanation_path: Start with the quote as a quote: on stage in Abu Dhabi the CEO said the new model is "above the Chinese models on certain aspects", and Reuters recorded that he named no model and no benchmark, so the claim was unfalsifiable for three weeks while only the API existed. Establish what a model card is: the vendor's own primary record published beside the weights, the first place a claim becomes checkable. Read the card the way an engineer would: it prints an independent aggregate score, 26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and admits the leading Chinese open-weight models score higher; the wins are per-task, coding tied at 48% with GLM-5.3 and cyber ahead at 51%. Before the hardware beat lands, the viewer needs the two halves of a Mixture-of-Experts model: about 1T parameters exist but only about 52B compute per token, and every expert still has to sit in memory. Then the consequence: the smallest official quant is 233 GB, so the claim "you can run this at home" narrows to machines most viewers do not own. Payoff: the habit, not the verdict -- when a CEO says "beats", ask which benchmark, which model, whose measurement, and at what memory.

claims.claim: Mistral's CEO claimed on October 6, 2026 that the new model beats Chinese models, saying it is above them on "certain aspects, including cyber", without naming which models or benchmarks.
claims.source_title: France's Mistral launches AI model it says outperforms some Chinese rivals (Reuters)

claims.claim: Mistral's own model card states the architecture as "~1T total / ~52B active parameters", a Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts of which 4 are active per token plus 1 shared expert, and a 1M token context window.
The model card itself prints an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 score of 26 and states that the leading open-weight models from China score higher on that aggregate index.
On coding the card prints 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, "effectively tied" with the Chinese model GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.

Independent harness Artificial Analysis confirms the Intelligence Index score of 26, lists the model at 1.1T total and 52B active parameters, and measures output speed of 161.3 tokens per second on Mistral's API, not local hardware.
claims.source_title: Mistral Large 4 (high) - Intelligence, Performance & Price Analysis (Artificial Analysis)

claims.claim: The open-weight release post claims the clearest per-task win, cyber: 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, alongside an average refusal rate of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests.
claims.source_title: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight

claims.claim: The smallest published GGUF quantization is 233 GB (1-bit) requiring a 256 GB RAM device, 2-bit runs 302-378 GB on 384-512 GB, and near full precision Q8 is 1.1 TB on 1.2 TB+.
Transformers shipped day-one support in release v5.22.0 titled "Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)", published 29 Oct 14:15, the same day the weights landed.

analogy_candidates.mapping: One benchmark is one judge's card, another judge scores it for the other side, and the CEO quote is the promoter's press conference, not the decision.
analogy_candidates.limit: A title fight still crowns one winner, while aggregate-versus-per-task benchmarks can both be true at once, so "beats" depends on which card you are shown.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: All-star roster versus the eleven on the pitch
analogy_candidates.mapping: About 1T parameters are the squad, about 52B active are who actually touches each token, and a bigger squad costs more to keep under contract.
analogy_candidates.limit: Benched players cost nothing on match day, whereas every one of the 1T weights must sit in your RAM even though only about 52B compute per token.

misconceptions.reality: Mistral's own model card says the leading Chinese open-weight models score higher than its 26 on the aggregate Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5; the honest version is per-task -- tied with GLM-5.3 on coding at 48%, ahead on cyber at 51%.

misconceptions.myth: If it is open weights, you can run it at home like a Qwen download.
misconceptions.reality: The smallest published GGUF is 233 GB at 1-bit, which does not fit a 24 GB gaming GPU or a 128 GB machine; open weights here means downloadable, not runnable at home.

glossary.definition: The downloadable numbers a model is made of, so anyone can run it on their own hardware instead of renting access through the maker's API.
An architecture that splits a model into many specialist sub-networks called experts and routes each token through only a few of them.
The slice of the model that actually computes for a given token, for example about 52B of about 1T total.
The document a vendor publishes beside the weights listing architecture, license and benchmark scores; the primary record for any claim.
An independent benchmarking site that runs named harnesses across models and publishes scores like its Intelligence Index v5.
One blended score built from many benchmarks, which can rank a model mid-pack even when it wins single tasks.
Shrinking model weights to fewer bits each so the file gets smaller, at some cost in quality.
The single-file format llama.cpp tools load, with size names like Q8_0 that tell you the bits and rough quality tier.

unverified: No measured local tokens-per-second for Mistral Large 4 on consumer hardware existed as of the morning the weights landed; the only throughput number found is API-based, so any at-home speed figure is an expectation.
Which Chinese models the CEO meant is unconfirmed: he named none, and GLM-5.3 is the leader named on the Coding Agent Index, not a confirmed referent of the quote.
Whether the 1-bit 233 GB quant actually fits and runs within 256 GB once the KV cache at long context is added is unstated in the sources fetched.
The CEO quote is verified only through Reuters' text; no video transcript was fetched.
suggested_outline:
The quote with nothing under it: "above the Chinese models on certain aspects", no model named, no benchmark named, and for three weeks nobody outside Mistral could check.
Run the receipt on the model card's own numbers: Intelligence Index 26 with Chinese open-weight leaders above it, coding tied at 48% with GLM-5.3, cyber won at 51% -- "beats" is true per-task and false overall.
What "open weights" costs you: about 1T total with ~52B active means every expert sits in memory; 233 GB at 1-bit, 1.1 TB at Q8, so no 24 GB GPU and no 128 GB Mac -- and next time a CEO says "beats", ask which benchmark, which model, whose measurement.
notes: Conflicts, recorded not averaged: the October 6 preview blog prints a "combined Coding Agent Index score of 49.8%" ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max, while the October 29 model card and OSS post print 48% "effectively tied" with GLM-5.3; these describe different checkpoints (three more weeks of reinforcement learning) and different comparison sets, and the October 29 figures are treated as current. Artificial Analysis lists total parameters as 1.1T where the model card says ~1T; both are kept verbatim, each attributed. Thin spot: most benchmark numbers on the model card are vendor-cited even when the harness is named; the only independently measured page fetched is Artificial Analysis, and its 161.3 tokens-per-second is API-based, not local. Reuters spells the CEO "Artur Mensch" (Oct 6 story) and "Arthur Mensch" (Oct 29 story); each quote keeps its own story's spelling.
viewer_situation: You have a gaming PC or a Mac, you saw the headline that a French model beats the Chinese ones, and you have never opened a model card to check a claim like that yourself.
objection: An aggregate index is itself just a weighted bucket of someone's chosen benchmarks, so trading the 26 for a per-task 51% is cherry-picking in the opposite direction.
